questions.question: Explain how does time management help in reducing stress?
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how does time management help in reducing stress?
  • Effective time management is a key tool for stress prevention and maintaining a holistic
  • lifestyle.
  • Techniques: (3 marks)
  • • Prioritization: Use tools like the Eisenhower Matrix (urgent vs. important) to
  • focus on tasks that truly matter.
  • • Goal Setting : Set SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time -
  • bound) goals for better direction.
  • • Planning: Use daily planners, calendars, or apps to organize tasks and
  • deadlines.
  • • Time Blocking : Assign specific time slots for tasks to avoid multitasking and
  • distractions.
  • • Avoid Procrastination : Break large tasks into smaller, manageable steps to
  • overcome inertia.
  • • Set Realistic Limits: Learn to say “no” when overcommitted.
  • Benefits: (2 marks)
  • • Reduces stress and panic by avoiding last-minute rushes.
  • • Increases productivity and work-life balance.
  • • Provides a sense of control and achievement.
  • • Frees up time for self-care and relaxation activities.

questions.question: Classify antioxidants with examples. [5x4 = 20] Part D Essay Each question carries 10 marks
questions.solution_html:
• Classify antioxidants with examples.
  • Classification – (4 marks) , Examples – (1 mark)
  • Antioxidants can be classified into two major types based on their origin:
  • A. ENDOGENOUS ANTIOXIDANTS (Produced within the body)
  • These are naturally synthesized by the body to protect against oxidative damage. They
  • include:
  • • Enzymatic antioxidants:
  • o Superoxide dismutase (SOD): Converts harmful superoxide radicals into less
  • harmful molecules.
  • o Catalase: Breaks down hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen.
  • o Glutathione peroxidase: Neutralizes peroxides and protects membranes from
  • lipid peroxidation.
  • • Non-enzymatic antioxidants:
  • o Glutathione: A tripeptide present in most cells; acts as a powerful detoxifier
  • and antioxidant.
  • o Uric acid and bilirubin also act as natural antioxidants in the body.
  • B. EXOGENOUS ANTIOXIDANTS (Obtained from diet)
  • These are antioxidants we get from food , especially fruits, vegetables, nuts, and whole
  • grains. Examples include:
  • • Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid) – Found in citrus fruits, amla, guava, bell peppers.
  • • Vitamin E (Tocopherol) – Found in nuts, seeds, vegetable oils, and green leafy
  • vegetables.
  • • Carotenoids – Like beta-carotene, lycopene, lutein found in carrots, tomatoes, and
  • spinach.
  • • Polyphenols and flavonoids – Found in tea, cocoa, grapes, berries, apples.
  • • Selenium and zinc – Trace minerals that work as cofactors in antioxidant enzyme
  • systems.
  • Part D
  • Essay Questions
  • Each question carries (10 marks)

questions.question: Describe in detail the internal (endogenous) and external (exogenous) processes that contribute to free radical production.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe in detail the internal (endogenous) and external (exogenous) processes
  • processes that contribute to free radical production.
  • A. Internal (Endogenous) Sources of Free Radicals (5 marks)
  • These originate within the body during normal physiological processes.
  • • Normal Metabolic Processes:
  • o Occur during cellular respiration in mitochondria.
  • o Partial reduction of oxygen produces Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) such as
  • superoxide radical (O₂•⁻).
  • • Immune System Response:
  • o White blood cells (e.g., macrophages) produce free radicals like nitric oxide
  • and superoxide to destroy pathogens.
  • o Excess production can damage body tissues.
  • • Inflammation:
  • o Inflammatory reactions release enzymes and reactive compounds that generate
  • free radicals.
  • B. External (Exogenous) Sources of Free Radicals (5 marks)
  • These are generated from external environmental or lifestyle factors.
  • • Pollution:
  • o Air pollutants (vehicle exhaust, industrial smoke) introduce chemicals that
  • trigger free radical formation.
  • • Cigarette Smoke:
  • o Contains thousands of chemicals and free radicals.
  • o Promotes free radical production in lungs and bloodstream.
  • • Radiation (UV rays, X-rays):
  • o Splits molecules in skin and tissues, forming radicals.
  • o Leads to skin aging, DNA damage, and cancer risk.
  • • Processed Foods and Alcohol:
  • o High-fat, high-sugar foods and alcohol metabolism generate free radicals and
  • increase oxidative stress.
  • • Certain Medications and Chemicals:
  • o Drugs (e.g., chemotherapy), pesticides, and toxins increase radical production
  • during metabolism or tissue interaction.

questions.question: Discuss the definition, goals, and importance of holistic nutrition. [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the definition, goals and importance of holistic nutrition.
  • Definition:
  • “Holistic nutrition is a comprehensive approach to nutrition that considers the individual's
  • entire well-being, including physical, mental, emotional, and spiritual aspects, rather than just
  • focusing on dietary restrictions or specific nutrient needs. It emphasizes a personalized
  • approach to health, taking into account individual needs, preferences, and lifestyle
  • factors.” (3 marks)
  • Goals: (3.5 marks)
  • • To support complete health—physical, mental, emotional, and spiritual.
  • • To prevent diseases and promote long-term well-being.
  • • To nourish the body using whole, natural, and unprocessed foods.
  • • To provide personalized nutrition based on individual needs and preferences.
  • • To encourage a healthy and mindful relationship with food.
  • • To create harmony between food, lifestyle, and the environment.
  • Importance: (3.5 marks)
  • • It improves total wellness by focusing on the whole person, not just physical health.
  • • It promotes better lifestyle choices including sleep, exercise, and stress control.
  • • It helps reduce stress by supporting emotional balance and mental clarity.
  • • It reduces the use of unhealthy, processed foods by encouraging natural eating.
  • • It boosts digestion and strengthens the immune system.
  • • It supports sustainable living and responsible use of natural resources.
